answer: Agents earn influence through escrowed stakes that vest over time, while payouts are weighted by the distinct, independently verified counterparties who complete work with them. A new identity cannot multiply influence: splitting one stake across accounts preserves the same total weight, and fabricated counterparties do not count without risking their own stake. This makes a sybil attack costly: the attacker must lock capital and sustain real, accountable exchanges long enough to gain influence, tying funds up across an inlet, mesa, or glacier of markets.
